pr.title: Avoid a cast in `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(_mut)`
pr.description:
Casting to `*const ()` or `*mut ()` is no longer needed after https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/123840 so let's make the MIR smaller (and more inline-able, as seen in the tests).

If [ACP#362](https://github.com/rust-lang/libs-team/issues/362) goes through we can keep calling `ptr::from_raw_parts(_mut)` in these also without the cast, but that hasn't had any libs-api attention yet, so I'm not waiting on it.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: PR #124795 is explicitly a MIR-size/inlining optimization, not a semantic bug fix. Both implementations of `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(_mut)` construct the same wide raw slice pointer: the old form via `from_raw_parts(_mut)(data.cast(), len)` and the new form via `intrinsics::aggregate_raw_ptr(data, len)`. The removed `PtrToPtr` cast to `*const ()`/`*mut ()` and the extra `from_raw_parts` scope do not change any defined pointer metadata or runtime value. Therefore no source-grounded pair of ordinary Rust functions can satisfy the required criterion that original and transformed implementations produce different values under Miri for identical defined inputs. The patch’s changed evidence is limited to MIR dump/inlining expectations, and manufacturing a semantic difference such as changing the length, metadata, or return value would not encode the historical transformation.

analysis.summary: Removing the redundant cast to `*const ()`/`*mut ()` inside `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(_mut)` makes the generated MIR smaller and allows `slice_from_raw_parts(_mut)` to inline to an empty scope, which in turn enables more inlining of callers such as `Vec` drop and slice indexing. The PR replaces `from_raw_parts(data.cast(), len)` / `from_raw_parts_mut(data.cast(), len)` with the direct `intrinsics::aggregate_raw_ptr(data, len)` intrinsic. This is an optimization, not a correctness fix: the cast form was semantically valid but bloated MIR with an extra `PtrToPtr` cast and `from_raw_parts` scope.
analysis.originalLogic: `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts<T>(data: *const T, len: usize) -> *const [T]` was implemented as `from_raw_parts(data.cast(), len)`, and `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts_mut<T>(data: *mut T, len: usize) -> *mut [T]` as `from_raw_parts_mut(data.cast(), len)`. In both, `data.cast()` first converts the thin typed pointer to `*const ()` / `*mut ()` before metadata is attached.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pre-change implementation inserted a redundant thin-pointer cast `data as *const ()` / `data as *mut ()` (`PtrToPtr`) and then assembled the wide slice pointer via `from_raw_parts(_mut)`. This extra cast and nested `from_raw_parts` scope bloated MIR; `slice_from_raw_parts_mut` did not inline to an empty scope, and callers retained extra MIR statements such as `_8 = _7 as *const () (PtrToPtr); _0 = *const [u32] from (_8, _5);` instead of directly using `_0 = *const [u32] from (_7, _5);`. The corrected form avoids the cast and uses `intrinsics::aggregate_raw_ptr(data, len)` directly.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust code that forms a raw slice pointer from a thin typed pointer and a length via `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts` or `ptr::slice_from_raw_parts_mut`, including callers in `slice::get_unchecked_mut` for `Range`, `Vec::deref` to `&[u8]`, `slice_ptr_get_unchecked_range`, pointer `cast`, and `Vec` drop glue. The data pointer is to a sized `T`, and the metadata is a `usize` length.
analysis.trigger: Any call to `slice_from_raw_parts(_mut)` on a path that is being optimized/inlined, especially in slice indexing/deref and `Vec` drop elaboration, where the old cast prevented or enlarged the inlined MIR.
preconditions: The data pointer is a thin pointer to a sized type `T` and the metadata is a `usize` length.
The compiler supports assembling a raw wide pointer directly from a thin typed pointer without first casting to a unit pointer, as provided by the change referenced in the PR description.
The comparison is between two implementations of the same public function: one using `from_raw_parts(data.cast(), len)` and one using `intrinsics::aggregate_raw_ptr(data, len)`.
pitfalls: The old cast was not a miscompile; it was a MIR-size and inlining optimization. Do not classify this as a correctness bug fix.
Do not claim any compiler was built or that behavior was executed/reproduced; the evidence is MIR dump test expectations and library source changes.
The changed test expectations are not evidence of a new compiler pass: this PR edits library code, and the Inline test changes are consequences of the smaller MIR/inlining.
Do not generalize from the old cast to all pointer casts: the issue is specifically casting to `*const ()`/`*mut ()` before attaching slice metadata.
The PR notes that `ptr::from_raw_parts(_mut)` may also become usable without a cast if ACP#362 is accepted; that is future work, not part of this change.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR dump tests (e.g. under `tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen` and `tests/mir-opt/inline`) on small functions that call `slice_from_raw_parts(_mut)`. Construct two programs identical except for the transformation: one lowers through `from_raw_parts(data.cast(), len)` and the other through `aggregate_raw_ptr(data, len)`. In the pre-codegen MIR, assert the cast version contains a `PtrToPtr` cast to `*const ()`/`*mut ()` and a nested `from_raw_parts` scope, while the corrected version directly assigns e.g. `_0 = *const [u32] from (_7, _5);` with no unit-pointer temporary. Check that `slice_from_raw_parts_mut` and related scopes are inlined and empty, and that callers such as `Vec` drop show additional inlined scopes. Run for both panic-abort and panic-unwind configurations where the MIR tests provide them.
evidence: Casting to `*const ()` or `*mut ()` just bloats the MIR, so let's not.
If [ACP#362](https://github.com/rust-lang/libs-team/issues/362) goes through we can keep calling `ptr::from_raw_parts(_mut)` in these also without the cast
